source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with symbolic solvers for faithful logical reasoning
finding: LLM translates the problem into logic; a solver (Prover9, Z3, python-constraint, pyke) reasons. Beats standard prompting and chain-of-thought (CoT) on 4 of 5 datasets with GPT-4.
numbers: GPT-4 accuracy Standard / CoT / Logic-LM: ProofWriter 52.67/68.11/79.66; FOLIO 69.11/70.58/78.92; LogicalDeduction 71.33/75.25/87.63; AR-LSAT 33.33/35.06/43.04. Average gain over standard 39.2 pts (GPT-3.5), over CoT 18.4 pts (GPT-3.5).
limits: Not on every set: on PrOntoQA GPT-4 CoT 98.79 beat Logic-LM 83.20. Failed translations fall back to CoT.
agent_relevance: Pair a code solver with a translation step on constraint-style problems; keep CoT as the fallback.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with symbolic solvers for faithful logical reasoning
finding: The bottleneck is translation, not solving. Syntax success is near 100% on synthetic data but low on real expert-written problems.
numbers: GPT-4 executable rate: ProntoQA/ProofWriter/LogicalDeduction about 99-100%; FOLIO 79.9%; AR-LSAT 32.6% (GPT-3.5: 11.3%). Accuracy on executable AR-LSAT samples 60.0%.
limits: Executable is not the same as correct. Authors show a wrong constraint (below read as above).
agent_relevance: Cannot trust a solver verdict if the encoding is unchecked (G3). Check the encoding with held-out facts.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with symbolic solvers for faithful logical reasoning
finding: Solver advantage grows with reasoning depth. Solver error messages repair syntax but not meaning.
numbers: Logic-LM over CoT on ProofWriter by depth 0/1/2/4/5: +7.1/+5.0/+12.7/+20.0/+39.4 pts. Self-refinement raised executable rate by 5.01 on average (GPT-4 FOLIO executable 79.9 to 85.8, accuracy +0.5).
limits: Refinement rounds raise executable rate but accuracy plateaus.
agent_relevance: Revise from real solver output (G2) for syntax; semantics need a separate check.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SatLM: Satisfiability-aided language models using declarative prompting
finding: Declarative specification plus SAT/SMT solver beats imperative program-of-thought on constraint-heavy tasks (code-davinci-002, greedy).
numbers: SatLM / CoT / ProgLM: GSM-Sys 69.4/46.5/43.4; LSAT 35.0/23.5/n.a.; BoardgameQA 79.4/60.7/n.a.; CLUTRR 68.3/40.8/58.9; ProofWriter depth 5 99.7/80.1/83.7; ALGEBRA 77.5/53.6/52.3.
limits: On plain GSM greedy, ProgLM 72.7 is slightly above SatLM 71.8: no gain when the task is not constraint-like.
agent_relevance: Use declarative, solver-checked specs when the task is a set of constraints.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SatLM: Satisfiability-aided language models using declarative prompting
finding: The solver gives a usable abstain signal: UNSAT and AMBIG results flag a bad specification. Selective accuracy is much higher than the program baseline.
numbers: Selective accuracy SatLM vs ProgLM: GSM-Sys 77.1 vs 45.2; GSM 77.2 vs 73.8; CLUTRR 89.9 vs 73.7. Coverage fell: GSM-Sys 90.0 vs 95.8; CLUTRR 76.0 vs 79.9. CLUTRR SatLM outputs: UNSAT 3.5%, AMBIG 15.5%.
limits: One round only; authors did not re-prompt on UNSAT or AMBIG. Quantifiers and nonlinear arithmetic are costly for the solver.
agent_relevance: Strong fit for S4/S7: treat UNSAT as inconsistent spec and AMBIG as under-constrained, then re-ask the model.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SatLM: Satisfiability-aided language models using declarative prompting
finding: With self-consistency (SC), SatLM gains persist on logic; the arithmetic edge narrows.
numbers: SatLM with SC: GSM-Sys 80.9; GSM 84.8; ALGEBRA 90.9; LSAT 37.4 (prior SoTA 30.9); BoardgameQA 80.7 (prior 73.9); CLUTRR 80.1; ProofWriter 99.7. ProgLM with SC: GSM-Sys 53.4, CLUTRR 71.9.
limits: Only 5 samples on LSAT, BoardgameQA and ProofWriter because prompts are long.
agent_relevance: Samples plus a solver filter compound: agreement is a hint, the solver is the check (G4).

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: neurosymbolic approach to logical reasoning with LLMs and first-order provers
finding: Independent test of translate-then-prove with Prover9 and 10-way majority voting. Mixed: big win on synthetic ProofWriter, no win for GPT-4 on real-language FOLIO.
numbers: FOLIO GPT-4: CoT 75.3 vs LINC 72.5 (McNemar p=0.58, not significant). FOLIO GPT-3.5: LINC 62.6 vs closest baseline 54.9. FOLIO StarCoder+: LINC 56.0 vs best baseline 41.8. ProofWriter balanced subset: GPT-3.5 96.4, GPT-4 98.3 with LINC.
limits: A partial non-replication of the strong Logic-LM FOLIO gain at GPT-4. Bar values read from figure text.
agent_relevance: Tools help weaker models most; for the strongest model the translation loss can cancel the gain.

source: Olausson et al. (2023) LINC: neurosymbolic approach to logical reasoning with LLMs and first-order provers
finding: Error analysis: LINC is more precise but less complete than CoT. It says Uncertain far more often because the formalisation drops unstated facts.
numbers: Predicted labels on FOLIO (GPT-4): CoT 32% True/27% False/41% Uncertain; LINC 24%/17%/57% (2% errors). Syntax errors in generated FOL: StarCoder+ 38%, GPT-3.5 24%, GPT-4 13%, mostly one symbol used with two arities.
limits: Failure L1: missing implicit facts such as Person(Harry). CoT failures: converse fallacy, stuck on long paths.
agent_relevance: Add a step that lists background facts to state before calling the solver; a missing fact reads as Unknown, not as an error.

source: Han et al. (2022, rev. 2024) FOLIO: natural language reasoning with first-order logic
finding: Benchmark with checked FOL annotations. It exposes the translation gap: syntax is easy, semantics is not.
numbers: NL-to-FOL few-shot: syntactic validity GPT-3.5 93.3, GPT-4 93.9; inference-engine execution accuracy 56.0 and 63.8. Test majority baseline 38.5%. A screen found 39.2% of stories had at least one problem and needed rewriting.
limits: Authors note FOL annotations can be error-prone and check them with an engine.
agent_relevance: FOLIO labels may themselves be wrong; a solver-vs-label disagreement needs a second look.

source: Han et al. (2022, rev. 2024) FOLIO
finding: Plain LLM accuracy on FOLIO and the lift from solver methods as summarised by the FOLIO authors.
numbers: Flan-T5-Large fine-tuned 65.7; LLaMA-13B 33.63 (chance 33); LLaMA-70B 43.97; GPT-3.5 58.34; LINC about +9 and Logic-LM/DetermLR more than +13 over few-shot GPT-4. NL-FOL execution accuracy GPT-4 on Wikipedia-seeded stories 75.43 vs hybrid template stories 53.10.
limits: Hybrid (template-derived) problems are harder to translate than Wikipedia-seeded ones.
agent_relevance: Translation difficulty varies by problem origin, so measure it on our own task mix.

source: Kirtania et al. (2024) Logic-LM++: multi-step refinement for symbolic formulations
finding: Re-runs Logic-LM and adds a pairwise-comparison backtracking agent that keeps a revised formalisation only if the LLM judges it better. Gains on FOLIO and AR-LSAT, none on ProofWriter with GPT-4.
numbers: GPT-4 Logic-LM vs Logic-LM++: FOLIO 78.92 vs 84.80; ProofWriter 79.66 vs 79.66; AR-LSAT 43.04 vs 46.32. GPT-3.5: FOLIO 62.80 vs 62.25 (slightly worse), AR-LSAT 26.41 vs 28.13. Backtracking added about 6 pts (GPT-4) and 3 (GPT-3.5).
limits: The keep/revert decision is an LLM judge, which conflicts with our rule that the model never grades itself. Logic-LM GPT-3.5 FOLIO listed as 62.80 vs 62.74 in the original.
agent_relevance: Semantic repair is possible but the judge is the weak link; replace it with a code check on held-out facts.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: on the scaling limits of LLMs for logical reasoning
finding: Pure LLM reasoning on constraint satisfaction (logic grid) puzzles collapses as the search space grows (the curse of complexity), even for reasoning models. Z3 conflict count is used as a difficulty measure.
numbers: Grid-level accuracy overall (small/medium/large/x-large): o1-full 81.0 (97.2/92.1/78.0/42.5); DeepSeek-R1 78.7; o1-preview 71.4 (x-large 17.0); o1-mini 59.7; best non-reasoning model Sonnet-3.5 36.2; GPT-4o x-large 0.0; Phi-3.5-4B 12.8.
limits: One puzzle family with a unique solution each. Models have moved on since.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for when to hand a puzzle to a code solver instead of reasoning in text.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic
finding: Test-time scaling helps only with an oracle picker; voting and self-verification give little. Hidden reasoning tokens track Z3 conflicts until a ceiling.
numbers: GPT-4o: pass@128 (BoN-Oracle) 69.1 vs greedy 31.7; majority vote N=32 38.0, N=128 37.6; best-of-N with reward model N=32 34.8. o1 hidden tokens about 5,200 vs about 500 for GPT-4o; about 400 tokens per Z3 conflict below 20 conflicts, plateau above 30.
limits: Oracle selection is not available at run time.
agent_relevance: Sampling only pays if a checker (a solver) can pick the right sample. A Z3 verifier is such a checker.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: benchmarking LLMs' logical reasoning via automated puzzle generation from SAT formulas
finding: 2,100 puzzles from random CNF with solver-validated labels. LLMs are weak at search-style reasoning, especially at showing UNSAT.
numbers: o4-mini: 78.0% on hard, 65.0% on hard UNSAT (chance 50). Mean over all models on hard: 53.0%; hard SAT 66.7%, hard UNSAT 39.3%. Easy 4-19 clauses, medium 20-30, hard 31-50.
limits: Puzzles are LLM-written stories of formulas; story fidelity is checked by LLM and solver but not perfect.
agent_relevance: An agent should not say consistent from text reasoning on 30+ interacting constraints; call the solver.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench
finding: Dominant error is satisfiability bias. A right label does not mean right reasoning.
numbers: Errors: satisfiability bias o4-mini 68.7%, DeepSeek-R1 40.5%; context inconsistency 17.0% / 44.7%; condition omission 14.3% / 12.6%. Trace correctness o4-mini 74.4, DS-R1 78.0, DS-V3 68.4, Claude-3.7 54.2, QwQ 52.4. Scaling plateaued near 50-53% on hard for Qwen3 and Llama families.
limits: Trace grading uses solver checks of the assignment or the UNSAT core.
agent_relevance: Require a witness (assignment) for SAT claims and a core for UNSAT claims, checked by code.

source: Lyu et al. (2023) Faithful chain-of-thought reasoning
finding: LLM writes a symbolic chain (Python, Datalog, PDDL); a deterministic solver runs it. Faithful by construction and better than CoT on 9 of 10 benchmarks.
numbers: Relative gain over CoT: +6.3% math word problems, +3.4% planning, +5.5% multi-hop QA, +21.4% CLUTRR (41.3% with SC). With GPT-4 and Codex: 95.0+ on 6 datasets. Removing NL comments on CLUTRR: -19.4 pts.
limits: StrategyQA stays below CoT, blamed on sparse Datalog in pretraining. Gains shrink with SC on math (GSM8K 9.0% to 2.6%). Human study: StrategyQA chains only 66.7% judged correct.
agent_relevance: Faithful is not correct: a solver faithfully executes a wrong translation.

source: Ganguly et al. (2024) Proof of Thought: neurosymbolic program synthesis allows robust and interpretable reasoning
finding: JSON-DSL compiled to Z3. On StrategyQA the system overpredicts true.
numbers: 1000 StrategyQA questions, 3 feedback loops: 82.4% compiled (17.6% failed); recall 91.40%, precision 58.22%, F1 71.13%, false positive rate 53.98%. In another test compile errors fell from 14.6% to 0% and win rate on compiled programs rose from 72% to 81.55%.
limits: Open-world commonsense fits logic poorly; weak evidence; no direct CoT accuracy comparison read.
agent_relevance: Solver checks suit explicit constraints, not commonsense questions.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Lemur: integrating LLMs in automated program verification
finding: LLM proposes loop invariants and an SMT-based verifier checks them (sound calculus). Large gains on hard verification tasks.
numbers: Code2Inv: ESBMC alone 68, Lemur(GPT-4) 107, Lemur(GPT-3.5) 103, Code2Inv 92 solved. 47 hard SV-COMP tasks: UAutomizer 1, ESBMC 1, Lemur(GPT-4) 25, Lemur(GPT-3.5) 14. Mean proposals 4.7 (Code2Inv) to 7.2 (SV-COMP); one task needed 90.
limits: Tasks were preselected where baselines failed; programs under 150 tokens; possible training-data overlap.
agent_relevance: Generate then verify with the solver as an unfakeable judge is the strongest pattern here (G2, G3).

source: Feng et al. (2025) VeriCoT: neuro-symbolic chain-of-thought validation via logical consistency checks
finding: Translates each CoT step to SMT-LIB with premises, and a solver checks validity. Verified chains are more accurate than average; verification feedback improves self-reflection and fine-tuning.
numbers: Self-reflection: average 46% relative gain in verification pass rate, 41% relative gain in verifiable correct outcomes. LegalBench-SARA (table as extracted, may misalign): VeriCoT pass rate 45.2, precision 94.1, task accuracy 81.4. Datasets: ProofWriter, LegalBench-SARA, BioASQ.
limits: Both formalisation and premise inference use an LLM, so a bad translation can pass or fail wrongly.
agent_relevance: Per-step consistency checking by code is a model for our S7 check.

source: Selsam et al. (2019) Learning a SAT solver from single-bit supervision (NeuroSAT)
finding: A neural net trained only on sat/unsat labels learns to find assignments and generalises to larger problems by running more iterations, but is not competitive with real solvers.
numbers: Test accuracy 85% on SR(40) (about 200 clauses); a satisfying assignment can be decoded for over 70% of satisfiable problems. Trained on 10-40 variables.
limits: Not competitive with state-of-the-art solvers (authors say so). Narrow random distribution.
agent_relevance: A learned guesser can propose; only a complete solver proves. Do not replace Z3 with a model.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs can't plan, but can help planning in LLM-Modulo frameworks
finding: Position paper: LLMs as idea generators with external sound critics and verifiers in a loop. Cites that only about 12% of LLM-generated plans were executable.
numbers: About 12% of plans from LLMs were executable without error in the cited planning study.
limits: Position paper plus cited results; no new experiment read.
agent_relevance: Same architecture as ours: model fills a slot, program verifies.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and fate: limits of transformers on compositionality
finding: Transformers solve multi-step compositional tasks by pattern matching, and error compounds with depth. Motivates offloading to exact procedures.
numbers: Accuracy decays with problem depth and size on multiplication, puzzle and dynamic-programming tasks (exact figures not extracted).
limits: Not about SAT directly. Context only.
agent_relevance: Explains why long text chains are risky and exact checkers matter.

source: Cross-study comparison: Logic-LM, LINC, Logic-LM++, SatLM
finding: Gains are large on synthetic shallow-language sets and shrink or vanish on real-language sets with a strong model.
numbers: GPT-4 FOLIO: Logic-LM 78.92, Logic-LM++ 84.80, LINC 72.5 vs CoT 70.58 (Logic-LM paper) or 75.3 (LINC paper). ProofWriter GPT-4: 79.66 (Logic-LM), 98.3 (LINC), 99.7 (SatLM, depth 5, code-davinci-002).
limits: Not like for like: different subsets, prompts, open vs closed world; CoT baselines differ by about 5 points.
agent_relevance: Expect big variance in reported gains; run our own head-to-head before relying on a tool.

source: Cross-study comparison: SATBench and ZebraLogic vs Logic-LM
finding: Text-only reasoning fails where solvers are strongest (many interacting constraints, UNSAT proofs); solver pipelines fail where language is messy (translation).
numbers: ZebraLogic x-large: GPT-4o 0.0, o1-full 42.5. SATBench hard UNSAT: mean 39.3, best 65.0. Logic-LM AR-LSAT GPT-4 executable only 32.6%.
limits: Different tasks and models; 2025 reasoning models are close to older tool-assisted numbers on small puzzles.
agent_relevance: Route by size: many interacting constraints go to a solver; otherwise reason in text. Always check the encoding.

source: SatLM result types: UNSAT, AMBIG, ERROR as separate signals
finding: Solver output type carries different information and should drive different next steps.
numbers: CLUTRR: AMBIG 15.5% vs UNSAT 3.5% of outputs. Wrong answers GSM-Sys: ProgLM 52.5% vs SatLM 20.6%.
limits: Single paper; code-davinci-002 for the main table.
agent_relevance: Map to schema: UNSAT revise facts; AMBIG ask for the missing constraint; ERROR fix syntax.
